checkedAlternates.risk: A goalkeeper uses hands, and throw-ins are taken by hand, so a literal player may argue for the hand row.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Soccer is the one game on the board where the ball is moved with the feet for almost the whole match, which is what makes it the single-item row.

checkedAlternates.risk: The bowler delivers the ball with a hand, and fielding is entirely by hand.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Scoring in cricket happens with the bat, which is the rule the row names, alongside baseball.

checkedAlternates.risk: A table tennis paddle is small and held like an extension of the hand.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A paddle is a racket, and the tennis and squash items anchor the row.

checkedAlternates.risk: A hockey stick has a head that can read as a racket face.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A stick strikes the ball rather than stringing a rebound, which is the bat and club row that golf and baseball anchor.

authorReview.notes: Every row names the thing that strikes the ball. Games where a hand touches the ball incidentally are still sorted by how a point is scored.

blindPlaytest.notes: If testers argue soccer belongs with hands because of the goalkeeper, relabel the first row as "Mostly with your feet".
